answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the river check immediately, the relic audit keeps the resolved set and the ember replay shows exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 296 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 296 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
